- If sentiment shows strong bullish (e.g., +1.00) in recent days, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment shows strong bearish (e.g., -1.00), model often under-forecasts; adjust downward bias or add early correction.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct — apply lagged mean reversion or cap forecast at 1–2 days above peak.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00/0.25), model often drifts toward mean reversion — align forecast with recent 5–7 day average if no strong sentiment.
- If true outcome shows strong divergence from forecast in first 5–7 days (e.g., >3% error), model may be overconfident — reduce forecast volatility or add early correction factor.
- Forecast horizon 30d often overestimates upward trend after low sentiment periods — apply sentiment-weighted smoothing or reduce slope if sentiment < 0.25.
- If sentiment turns negative after a peak, model often fails to anticipate drop — add early downward bias or trigger correction rule if sentiment drops below -0.5.
